literal: Before coming, he who guards not, life, before fire, straw stack like, will perish.
translation: The life of one who does not guard against a fault before it happens will perish like a haystack placed before a fire.
modern: குற்றம் வருவதற்கு முன்பே அதைக் காத்துக்கொள்ளாதவனுடைய வாழ்க்கை, நெருப்பின் முன்னால் வைக்கப்பட்ட வைக்கோல் போர் எரிந்து அழிவதைப் போல அழிந்துவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet warns of the danger of not anticipating and preventing faults. The phrase 'varu muṉṉar' (before it comes) emphasizes the need for foresight and proactive defense against errors. The word 'vai' means straw and 'tūṟu' means a stack or heap; together they form a haystack. Just as a dry haystack is instantly consumed when placed in front of a fire, the life and prosperity of a person who fails to guard against impending faults will be swiftly and completely destroyed.
